headline: Profits surge on higher oil prices as debt keeps shrinking
summary_short: Occidental earned $2.75 per diluted share (adjusted $2.40) in Q2 FY2026 on revenue of $8.07 billion, both up sharply from a year ago as worldwide realized crude prices jumped 38% q/q to $96.78/bbl, while long-term debt fell to $12.80 billion.
summary_long: Revenue rose 54.2% q/q and 53.4% y/y to $8.07B as worldwide realized crude prices jumped 38% q/q to $96.78/bbl and midstream & marketing swung to $1.3B of pre-tax income from an $87M loss on higher crude-sale-timing and gas-transportation margins. Diluted EPS was $2.75 (adjusted $2.40), down 12.1% q/q but up from $0.26 a year ago, when items affecting comparability weighed on results. Production averaged 1,433 Mboed, above the high end of guidance on Permian and Gulf of America outperformance. Occidental cut principal debt by $1.9B to $11.8B, raised its quarterly dividend 8% to $0.28/share, and generated $3.0B of free cash flow before working capital, the highest since Q3 2022.

drivers.explanation: Higher worldwide realized crude prices (+38% q/q to $96.78/bbl) and a midstream & marketing swing to pre-tax income on higher crude-sale-timing and gas-transportation margins.
Adjusted EPS of $2.40 tracks higher oil & gas pre-tax income from higher realized crude prices, partially offset by lower domestic natural gas prices.
Reflects the same oil & gas segment swing on higher realized crude prices plus midstream & marketing's return to profitability, per the segment result tables.
Consolidated pretax income tracks the oil & gas and midstream segment income swings described above, per the segment income schedule.
Cash grew as $4.27B of net operating cash inflow exceeded $2.15B of net financing outflow (mostly $1.79B of debt repayments) and $1.78B of investing outflow, per the cash-flow statement.
Debt fell on continued principal repayments ($1.79B of debt payments this quarter) following Q1's asset-sale-funded paydown, per the financing-activities section.
Growth was primarily retained-earnings accretion from the quarter's net income, partially offset by ongoing treasury-stock purchases, per the balance sheet.

Management highlighted an 8% dividend increase to $0.28/share, a $1.9B reduction in principal debt to $11.8B, and $3.0B of free cash flow before working capital — the highest since Q3 2022 — citing strong execution and advanced recovery capabilities.
